No Compromise: Why they can't be the one to transform, the risks involved, can they trust the Emperor? Some sub nodes should have different reactivity in the case they are already partial illithid, or were open to using the powers but never did

This dialog is about the avatar and what they should do, but the decision is not made here as it's possible the player can change their mind when they return to gameplay or talk to the Emperor. This is a discussion of their available options, their feelings towards them, and why the player needs to be the one to transform (exception being Karlach). Their is a risk the player may feel sour towards their team for the perceived cowardice, as almost all of them are not willing to transform. This dialog will need to sell why the player is the hero of this story.

context: The party has discovered that the avatar (and possibly others) carries an illithid tadpole — a parasite that can psychically influence people — and they've already experienced strange voices and even watched a similar parasite emerge from a corpse, resisting attempts to destroy it. They’ve also encountered mind‑flayer technology in the Tadpoling Centre and debated whether to free or purge pod occupants, while companions (for example Astarion) have floated the idea of trying to control the tadpole rather than simply destroying it. This scene is a group discussion weighing whether the player should accept transformation to use the tadpole’s power; companions are positioned to argue different stances (No Compromise, At Any Cost, Bridge) and certain allies (Karlach, Lae’zel in Orpheus’s case) have special stakes. The conversation doesn’t finalize the choice — it’s meant to probe risks, moral consequences, and the possibility of future resentment or even departure if the player decides to embrace illithid power.
